pr_title: fix(rust, python): respect startby in groupby_dynamic when every is greater than 1d
pr_body:
closes #9333 

The if-then condition was introduced in https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/2711 - but, as far as I can tell, that was when `groupby_dynamic` didn't have the option to specify `start_by`.
Since `groupby_dynamic` has `start_by`, I think it's a lot simpler to just truncate to the start of the window for `start_by='window'` (and to document what exactly that means for weeks, i.e. Monday) - if anyone wants to start by the first datapoint, as the original poster did in https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/2683, then they can just pass `start_by='datapoint'`

issue_context.title: groupby_dynamic doesn't truncate label when the number of periods is greater than 1
issue_context.body:
### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Issue description

The code below prints
```python
shape: (1, 2)
┌──────────────────────────────────┬───────────┐
│ ts                               ┆ values    │
│ ---                              ┆ ---       │
│ datetime[μs, Africa/Addis_Ababa] ┆ list[f64] │
╞══════════════════════════════════╪═══════════╡
│ 2000-01-01 03:00:00 EAT          ┆ [10.0]    │
└──────────────────────────────────┴───────────┘
shape: (1, 2)
┌──────────────────────────────────┬───────────┐
│ ts                               ┆ values    │
│ ---                              ┆ ---       │
│ datetime[μs, Africa/Addis_Ababa] ┆ list[f64] │
╞══════════════════════════════════╪═══════════╡
│ 2000-01-01 00:00:00 EAT          ┆ [10.0]    │
└──────────────────────────────────┴───────────┘

```

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.from_repr("""\
shape: (1, 2)
┌──────────────────────────────────┬────────┐
│ ts                               ┆ values │
│ ---                              ┆ ---    │
│ datetime[μs, Africa/Addis_Ababa] ┆ f64    │
╞══════════════════════════════════╪════════╡
│ 2000-01-01 03:00:00 EAT          ┆ 10.0   │
└──────────────────────────────────┴────────┘
""")
df = df.with_columns(pl.col('ts').set_sorted())
print(df.groupby_dynamic('ts', every='2d').agg(pl.col('values')))
print(df.groupby_dynamic('ts', every='1d').agg(pl.col('values')))
```


### Expected behavior

For '2d':
```python
shape: (1, 2)
┌──────────────────────────────────┬───────────┐
│ ts                               ┆ values    │
│ ---                              ┆ ---       │
│ datetime[μs, Africa/Addis_Ababa] ┆ list[f64] │
╞══════════════════════════════════╪═══════════╡
│ 1999-12-31 00:00:00 EAT          ┆ [10.0]    │
└──────────────────────────────────┴───────────┘
```

comments:
Seems like this is due to https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/2711

some notes to self before going to sleep:
- maybe that if-then statement can be removed, and then for weeks the default starting point would be `monday`
- maybe `'monday', `'tuesday'`, etc. can be removed as valid arguments to `start_by`, and `offset` can just be used to that effect anyway?

will come back to this

review_comments: before, the default `StartBy::Window` would actually act like `StartBy::DataPoint` for `'w'` - so, I'm explicitly setting `StartBy::DataPoint` to preserve the behaviour in the rest of the test
